**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ ۖ إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسْئُولًا﴾
… And fulfil completely every promise you have committed to. Allah will ask the one who made a promise about it on the Day of Resurrection, rewarding him if he kept it and fulfilled it, and punishing him if he betrayed it.

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَوْفُوا بِالْعُقُودِ﴾
O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: fulfil Allah's firm covenants, of believing in the laws of the religion and submitting to them, and fulfil the commitments you have to one another, of trusts, sales and other dealings, as long as they do not go against the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Marwan say to himself on that cold morning? And why did he get out of bed?
2. When the two boys invited him to the valley, why did he not leave Lu'ay to carry the water alone "for one day"? And how did he manage both his promise and the trip?
3. And what if Marwan had been ill that day? (Someone held back by a real excuse is not blamed, but he tells his friend before the meeting time, and does not leave him waiting in the cold.)

**This week's exercise**
Every day your child makes a small promise to someone in the family, with a set time (to lay the table after Asr, or to read to their little brother or sister before bed), and keeps it. Write down the promises they kept on a sheet of paper on the fridge.
